title: Power series over a field or a Cohen ring: complete regular local domain
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be either a field $k$, or a Cohen ring: a discrete valuation ring (a local principal ideal domain which is not a field) which is complete with respect to its maximal ideal and whose maximal ideal is generated by a prime number $p$ (Algebra, Definition 0327); write $\mathfrak m_\Lambda$ for the maximal ideal of $\Lambda$ ($0$ resp. $p\Lambda$). Let $d\ge0$ and $R_0=\Lambda[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Then: (1) $R_0$ is a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local integral domain with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_0=\mathfrak m_\Lambda R_0+(X_1,\ldots,X_d)$, i.e. $\mathfrak m_0=(X_1,\ldots,X_d)$ if $\Lambda=k$ and $\mathfrak m_0=(p,X_1,\ldots,X_d)$ if $\Lambda$ is a Cohen ring; (2) the composite $\Lambda\to R_0\to R_0/\mathfrak m_0$ induces an isomorphism $\Lambda/\mathfrak m_\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}R_0/\mathfrak m_0$; (3) $R_0$ is $\mathfrak m_0$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]; (4) $R_0$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] of Krull dimension $d$ if $\Lambda=k$ and $d+1$ if $\Lambda$ is a Cohen ring.

source.place: Algebra, Remark Tag 032C (remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary, line 45023), first two sentences (stated there without proof); Cohen ring: Definition Tag 0327 (definition-cohen-ring, line 44872)
